declaration-no-important.message: Avoid !important. Two deliberate exceptions ship, both in packages/core/src/reset.css and both explained in a comment beside the declarations they cover: `[hidden] { display: none !important }`, and the four declarations under `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`. This rule is switched off for that whole file by the override below, not by inline disables, so a NEW !important added there passes this gate silently: read the comment above the block you are editing before you add one. Anywhere else, change the rule you are writing rather than this guard. If you think the guard itself is wrong, open an issue.

selector-class-pattern.message: Class names must be either nave-kebab-case (global atoms) or camelCase (CSS Modules).

custom-property-pattern.message: Custom properties must begin with --nave-: every custom property Nave's own stylesheets declare or reference carries the namespace, so none can collide with a consumer's (R26). The bridge stylesheets are exempt through the override below, because they declare a UI library's own variable names and never a --nave- one (docs/04-adr/0003-layer-cascade-contract.md); a property-disallowed-list rule in that override holds the bridge's side instead.

property-disallowed-list.message: A bridge maps a UI library's own variable names onto Nave's tokens and never declares a --nave- name itself: @navecss/tokens writes those names in the same tokens.defaults layer, and the two never setting the same property is what makes the order between them irrelevant (docs/04-adr/0003-layer-cascade-contract.md). Read the Nave value through var(--nave-*) instead.
